aspects.says: A rejected message is compared with approved ones by each field's presence, length and kind of characters, because values differ between any two purchases.
basis: section:15.2. A Rejected Message Is Compared With Approved Ones by the Shape of Each Field

aspects.says: A packager's error names a field after the one that is wrong, so the search starts from the first field whose shape changed.
basis: section:15.2. A Rejected Message Is Compared With Approved Ones by the Shape of Each Field
aspects.reason: a pointer to unit 3, whose shifted-field example and practices grade it

aspects.says: Equal totals can hide differences that cancel, so every day is matched transaction by transaction by terminal and RRN.
basis: section:15.4. A Difference in Totals Is Explained Transaction by Transaction, Even When the Totals Agree

aspects.says: A logged message is found by its terminal, STAN and transmission time together, because STANs repeat across terminals and across days.
basis: section:15.1. A Message Is Named by Its Terminal, STAN and Transmission Time, and the Time Is UTC

aspects.says: The comparison is with approved messages of the same release and kind of purchase, and a shape any of them has is not a fault.
basis: section:15.2. A Rejected Message Is Compared With Approved Ones by the Shape of Each Field

aspects.says: An answer that adds, drops or rewrites a pairing field matches nothing and looks like silence, so pairing uses only fields every request carries and the host echoes unchanged.
basis: section:15.3.1. Spot the Problem: The Terminal Whose Approvals Never Arrived

aspects.says: A partial approval booked at the requested amount shows the terminal a full approval and leaves the merchant short by the difference.
basis: section:15.4. A Difference in Totals Is Explained Transaction by Transaction, Even When the Totals Agree

aspects.says: An unanswered request is placed by the last log that saw it; one that left is reversed wherever it stopped, and the place says what to fix.
basis: section:15.3. A Missing Answer Is Placed by the Last Log That Saw the Message

aspects.says: Field 11 names a message on one link only; across hops the transaction is asked for by its retrieval reference number.
basis: section:15.1. A Message Is Named by Its Terminal, STAN and Transmission Time, and the Time Is UTC
aspects.reason: which hop renumbers a message happens between companies and can't be run offline; unit c12's gateway practice grades the renumbering itself

aspects.says: A purchase carries the terminal's local date, the UTC transmission time and the settlement date, each for a different party.
basis: section:15.8. Design Note: Why a Purchase Carries Three Dates
aspects.reason: a design note explaining a choice of the standard; 15.1's practice grades the UTC transmission time it rests on

aspects.says: Field 7 holds the transmission time in UTC, while a log and fields 12 and 13 are local, so a ticket's time is matched against field 7.
basis: section:15.1. A Message Is Named by Its Terminal, STAN and Transmission Time, and the Time Is UTC
